source.author: verg
source.text: Parte alia fugiens amissis Troilus armis, infelix puer atque impar congressus Achilli, fertur equis, curruque haeret resupinus inani, lora tenens tamen; huic cervixque comaeque trahuntur per terram, et versa pulvis inscribitur hasta.
source.text_original: Parte alia fugiens amissis Troilus armis, / infelix puer atque impar congressus Achilli, / fertur equis, curruque haeret resupinus inani, / lora tenens tamen; huic cervixque comaeque trahuntur / per terram, et versa pulvis inscribitur hasta.
source.text_english: On the other side, Troilus is fleeing, his weapons lost, unhappy boy and no match for Achilles in battle; he is borne along by his horses, lying back upon his empty chariot, still gripping the reins. His neck and hair are dragged through the earth, and the dust is scored by his overturned spear.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: parte alia Pholoe multoque insanus Iaccho Rhoetus et Atracia subitae de virgine pugnae.
reuse.text_original: parte alia Pholoe multoque insanus Iaccho / Rhoetus et Atracia subitae de virgine pugnae.
reuse.text_english: On the other side Pholoe, and Rhoetus mad with much Bacchus, and Atrax because of the maiden’s sudden fight.
